attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No proof is known that an explicit high-q generator defeats all unary range-local transcripts and subthreshold residual corrections. High q may even help unary predicates by presenting many chances to hit a satisfiable generated formula.
steps: Instantiate H_N with M_N=N^q and L_N=(log N)^d, d>1, so SAT circuits of size L_N^c are N^{o(1)} after substitution.

Assume SAT in SIZE(n^c). Composing the SAT circuit with the bulk generator and the OR over M_N queries gives C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}; hence a valid H_N lower bound above N^{1+epsilon} contradicts every fixed c when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
Model nonuniform leakage by N^s predicates on t-tuples of generated formulas, each composed predicate costing N^{alpha+o(1)}. Dense enumeration gives N^{s+tq+alpha+o(1)} transcript cost.

If a size N^a aggregator plus residual correction of size N^lambda recovers H_N, then H_N has size N^{max{rho,s+tq+alpha,a,lambda}+o(1)}. Therefore any source lower bound must force this maximum to be at least 1+epsilon-o(1).

Choose q>(1+epsilon)/2. Since s,alpha>=0, every t>=2 dense tuple transcript has exponent s+tq+alpha>1+epsilon, so it cannot be a subthreshold falsifier. The audit collapses to t=1 transcripts and residual corrections.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument is a valid bridge and leakage cutoff only. It does not establish C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}; it merely identifies the precise remaining lower-bound target and one class of falsifiers that no longer needs auditing.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Static exact LP extension size is not a target-preserving proxy for adaptive polynomial-time computation.
steps: Encode a candidate NP-complete family as 0/1 polytopes P_n and prove rank_+(S(P_n))>n^k for every fixed k.
By Yannakakis, conclude P_n has no polynomial-size exact LP extended formulation.
Try to infer that no polynomial-time algorithm decides the encoded language.
This inference needs a compiler from arbitrary polynomial-time algorithms, or at least from polynomial-size circuits, into polynomial-size exact LP lifts for the same family.
The compiler is impossible in this generality: perfect matching is in P while xc(PM_m)=2^{Omega(m)}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a lower bound against LP_EF only. It gives no valid contradiction to SAT in P unless a special nonblack-box SAT-algorithm-to-EF transfer is supplied, and the general transfer is falsified by matching.

assumptions: P_n is a bounded polytope with a fixed facet-vertex slack matrix over rational data or an explicitly stated real-coefficient model.
The lower bound is for exact LP extended formulations, not separation oracles, SDP lifts, randomized algorithms, or Turing-machine decision procedures.
Input length is measured by the natural combinatorial encoding; for PM_m, the edge-coordinate dimension is e=binom(m,2).
definitions: source object: slack matrix S(P_n) of a 0/1 polytope family P_n, with rows indexed by facets and columns indexed by vertices; the source lower bound is nonnegative rank or extension complexity.
target object: exact polynomial-size linear extended formulations LP_EF(n^k), not Boolean SIZE(n^k) circuits, P/poly, or uniform polynomial-time algorithms.
controlled interface: Yannakakis factorization maps nonnegative factorizations of S(P_n) to LP extensions and back, preserving inequality count up to additive constants.
target-preserving condition: any claimed P-vs-NP transfer must provide an algorithm-to-EF compiler for the same encoded optimization problem; otherwise the valid target remains only LP_EF.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current source construction supplies a bounded-D, cap-compatible, non-natural certificate of a hard row. Aggregate-only lower bounds in the intermediate window are not target-preserving.
steps: Let F_m have M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)} distinct accepted tables T_{m,r}, and form G_m(r,x)=T_{m,r}(x).
A genuinely hard row immediately gives C(G_m)>2^{epsilon m}, because any circuit for G_m hardwired with r computes that row.
To infer a hard row from aggregate hardness alone, assume contrapositively that every row has a circuit of size at most S=2^{epsilon m}.
Without a shared circuit-output unranker, the only universal nonuniform simulation hardwires all row circuits and costs M_m*S=2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)}.
Therefore aggregate hardness below q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) can be explained by hard indexing, not row MCSP hardness.
If a small circuit-output unranker W exists, then G_m has size R+poly(S,m); so aggregate hardness separates into either row hardness or unranker hardness.
Combining with an aggregate access cap alpha_A gives the new viability inequality q_force<=alpha_A, equivalently D<=(alpha_A-epsilon)/(1-alpha_A).

All lower bounds discussed for rows and for G_m are against unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits unless a restricted source model is explicitly named.
A circuit-output unranker means a circuit family W_m(r,j) that outputs or evaluates a size-S circuit description for row r.
definitions: source object: a family F_m of accepted certificates whose distinct emitted truth tables T_{m,r}:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have canonical ranks r in [M_m], M_m <= 2^{D m+o(m)}, and are verified in 2^{O(m)} time without advice.
target object: an E-uniform language obtained from the multiplexed table G_m(r,x)=T_{m,r}(x), padded over kappa-dense source lengths, with desired unrestricted circuit lower bound 2^{delta n}.
controlled interface: E-canonical distinct-image unranking plus an audited ranked decoder; no nonuniform selector, advice string, or subthreshold random-access implementation may choose the hard row.

target-preserving condition: row hardness must be for unrestricted Boolean circuits at threshold 2^{epsilon m}, and ranking/padding overhead must preserve E-uniformity and the exponent delta < epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).

As D grows, q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) crosses the cap-compatible window, certifying that aggregate-only forcing is invalid.
held_fixed_controls: epsilon is a fixed positive row-hardness threshold, e.g. epsilon=0.45, and rows are tested against unrestricted Boolean circuits.
kappa=1 source-length density and E-canonical distinct-image ranking are held fixed.
No advice, nonuniform selector, or certificate-order ranking is allowed.
Aggregate access cap alpha_A=1/2 is used as the checkpoint-control benchmark.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route now hinges on whether aggregate decoder hardness certifies row MCSP hardness or merely hides rank-index complexity. A concrete probe is more informative than another abstract barrier citation.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Sparse linear-form carrier: choose an E-decidable sparse coefficient set S_m of size 2^{D m}; accepted images are T_a(x)=<a,x> mod 2 for a in S_m; the ranked decoder is G_m(r,x)=<unrank_{S_m}(r),x> mod 2. Every row has O(m)-size circuits, so any apparent MCSP no-side evidence must come from the unranking interface.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before this intuition may affect proof obligations, one must prove either a direct high-MCSP row certificate, or an aggregate lower bound at q_force that is below the declared cap alpha_A and cannot be attributed to circuit-output unranking hardness.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: D, the distinct-image entropy rate of the sparse coefficient set.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 35 identifies a sharper obstruction: low-image entropy D creates an index-hardness channel. The valid extraction exponent remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) from an actual hard row, but aggregate-only row forcing needs q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) and must also satisfy q_force<=alpha_A. Thus, with alpha_A=1/2, D<=1-2epsilon is mandatory; near the cap only D=o(1) is viable. This is route-level progress and a falsifier for aggregate shortcuts, not a proof of P != NP.
